PullRequest.Title: Update copilotUpgrade path for GitHub settings
PullRequest.Body:
Uses a more direct URL for Copilot pro checkout page to reduce number of redirect hops and improve load time for user.

[Internal Issue](https://github.com/github/licensing/issues/4276)

Scenarios.Scenario: A free or quota-limited Copilot user invokes “Upgrade to GitHub Copilot Pro” from the chat title bar, model picker, quota notification, status dashboard, or command palette.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command synchronously resolves the selected GitHub/GHE base URL, appends the return_to parameter, and calls IOpenerService.open once. The external browser’s network navigation must then load the signup page for the user to proceed; entitlement refresh occurs only after the user later returns focus and is unchanged by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: IOpenerService opens the resolved GitHub or GitHub Enterprise upgrade URL in an external browser, which performs the page navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one navigation per explicit upgrade command invocation, independent of workspace size, chat history, model count, or entitlement collection size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command called the same opener once with github-copilot/upgrade plus identical utm_source and return_to parameters; the diff only substitutes github-copilot/pro/signup as the path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The browser page load is the user-visible critical path to beginning checkout, although the VS Code command itself does not await the navigation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales only with the number of explicit upgrade-command invocations; there is no collection-driven multiplicity or automatic hot-path execution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One external navigation is issued per explicit command invocation. There is no loop, batch, or new parallelism; repeated user clicks can create repeated navigations exactly as before, with no diff-introduced concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache participates in URL resolution or external navigation. Cold and warm browser/network cache behavior may differ, but the diff neither changes cache keys controlled by VS Code nor adds retries, negative caching, or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff changes only the path string used by one existing user-triggered external navigation and leaves call count, scheduling, serialization, and retained state unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not establish server-side redirect counts or comparative endpoint latency, so the claimed load-time improvement cannot be independently quantified from code; this uncertainty does not reveal a regression mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The change preserves one network navigation per user action and may reduce server-side redirects, but repository evidence is insufficient to record a concrete regression fix with blame.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the sole changed hunk and traced its only consumer through GitHub/GHE URL resolution, return URL construction, opener invocation, and post-navigation entitlement refresh. No changed CPU, allocation, retention, I/O cardinality, concurrency, cache lifecycle, or critical-path scheduling mechanism warrants a performance finding.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
